title: Canary traffic-shift upgrade for private runtime with automated rollback and KV-cache warming
creator: Anjali Rao
description: Background: Private (VPC/on-prem) customers run a Redwood data-plane runtime that must be upgraded with zero-to-minimal customer disruption. Existing approaches are manual and have caused transient 5xx spikes during kernel/quantization rollout and KV cache churn. This ticket specifies an automated canary traffic-shift rollout for private runtime upgrades that integrates with our Terraform IaC, health probes, and the smart routing layer. The goal is deterministic, reversible upgrades with measurable SLO preservation and automated rollback triggers.
proposed_solution: Implement a phased canary controller that: (1) provisions a small canary cohort via Terraform module (isolated ASG/node pool or VM subset), (2) deploys new runtime artifact to canary nodes, (3) warms KV caches using replayed request prefixes, (4) shifts a configurable percentage of traffic via the smart router to canaries while evaluating SLOs and health checks, (5) progressively increases traffic to 100% if criteria met, otherwise performs an automated rollback that re-routes traffic and scales down canaries. All steps are orchestrated by a new 'private-upgrade' Terraform module + controller that emits audit logs and exposes runbooks via the Console.
rollout_steps: Step 0 - Preflight: run IaC plan checks, validate artifact signatures, ensure infra quotas and node image compatibility
Step 1 - Provision canary cohort: Terraform module creates dedicated small node pool (3-5 nodes) in customer's VPC using existing private modules
Step 2 - Deploy runtime: kube/agent rolling deploy to canary nodes with feature flags to enable new kernels
Step 3 - Cache warm: run KV cache warmer job that replays representative prefix traces from anonymized traces store
Step 4 - Smoke gating: health probes (startup, readiness, perf-baseline) must pass for 5m with stable metrics
Step 5 - Traffic shift 5%: router routes 5% of traffic to canaries, monitor for 15m
Step 6 - Progressive ramp: increase 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with stable interval checks and extended monitoring windows
Step 7 - Finalize: decommission old cohort via Terraform and publish upgrade completion audit
rollback_plan: Automated rollback trigger conditions: error-rate > 0.5% absolute increase, p95 latency regression > 30% or repeated readiness failures on canary nodes
Rollback actions: immediately shift traffic back to golden cohort, scale down canary node pool to zero via Terraform apply, mark rollout as failed and attach logs
Post-rollback diagnostics: collect full traces, kernel metrics, KV hit ratios, and produce an incident bundle for oncall
Manual rollback override: runbook steps for SRE to force rollback or hotfix artifact pinning
monitoring_signals: KV cache hit ratio and warmed-key count
GPU utilization and mem pressure per node
Model output regression checks (via small prompt set), scalar quality metrics
Node readiness/failure counts and crashloop indicators
acceptance_criteria: Canary module deploys end-to-end with Terraform plan and apply reproducibly in CI
Automated KV warming reduces cold-start token latency by >=25% on canary compared to baseline
Controller performs traffic shift and uses configured health gates to progress without manual intervention
Automated rollback executes within 2 minutes of trigger detection and restores baseline SLOs
Audit logs and rollout timeline available in Console for at least 90 days
Unit/integration tests for controller and canary Terraform module covered in CI with >=90% pass rate
risks: Cross-VPC networking edge-cases where canary cohort cannot reach upstream services leading to false-positive failures
KV warming could leak sensitive prefixes if trace anonymization fails
Terraform drift between operator-run and manual changes may lead to orphaned nodes
Rollback under heavy load may cause transient capacity pressure on golden cohort
